short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Volt measures one hundred and thirty eight volts on a resistor and one hundred and eighty four on an inductor, from a two hundred and thirty volt supply.
They're ninety degrees apart, so they add like arrows. The impedance triangle shows it: thirty and forty make fifty.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: In AC, the inductor's voltage peaks a quarter cycle before the resistor's. Since they don't peak together, you can't just add the numbers. You add them like arrows at right angles.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: AC voltages add as phasors, never as plain numbers.

short_scenes.say: Watch the full video: Impedance in AC!
short_scenes.narration: For the detailed explanation, watch the full video on our channel. It's part of our complete Network Theory course.
